assumptions: GIẢ ĐỊNH - LILYGO GPIO: the pins come from the LilyGO T-Display-S3 pin_config (LCD D0-D7 = 39,40,41,42,45,46,47,48; WR 8, RD 9, DC 7, CS 6, RST 5, BL 38, POWER_ON 15; BTN 0/14; IIC SDA 18 / SCL 17; touch INT 16 / RST 21, unused on the non-touch board). The firmware team checks these against the 2024-04-29 schematic. Assumed: header pins labelled 17, 18, 21, 3V and GND exist on the owner's board. CHECKLIST-RAP: the silkscreen labels must match. If 17/18/21 are not on the header, use GPIO1/2/3 by changing only the config header and WIRING.md.

GIẢ ĐỊNH - owned LILYGO already has pin headers soldered and a clear shell (seen in the owner's photo). The envelope is 66 x 28 x 23 mm including the downward Dupont housings, not measured. The case reconciles with the LILYGO STEP before the coupon print. Button positions are estimated from the photo only (both buttons on top at the USB-C end).

GIẢ ĐỊNH - PCA9685 uses the Adafruit layout (62.2 x 25.4 mm, address 0x40, 10k I2C pull-ups to VCC). VCC comes from 3V3 so I2C stays at 3.3 V. Never power VCC from 5 V. Height with servo plugs fitted is about 22 mm, not measured.

GIẢ ĐỊNH - KK10 WS2812 bar is about 51 x 10.2 x 3.5 mm (Adafruit 8-stick class), seen in the listing photo only. Its input pads may need 3 short wire solder joints, the only soldering in the build, listed in WIRING.md. The 3.3 V data line runs straight from GPIO21. If the LEDs flicker (CHECKLIST-RAP): first shorten the DIN wire and keep it beside GND. If that does not help, move the bar's 5V wire to the LILYGO 3V pin and keep brightness at 20% or less (firmware cap). No extra part.

GIẢ ĐỊNH - power bank criteria: 2 USB-A outputs, each ≥ 2.4 A, at most 100 x 65 x 15 mm and 120 g, ports on a short end, no auto-off with low current or a long auto-off delay. Purchase cables: (1) a short 90-degree USB-A to USB-C cable for the LILYGO, (2) a USB-A male to 2-wire (red/black, tinned ends) 5 V cable into the PCA9685 screw terminal. The plug zone allows about 22 mm of rigid plug length. If the plugs are longer, choose a shorter power bank (checklist).

Flashing: the LILYGO USB-C stays connected to the L-cable. To flash, the owner pulls that cable's USB-A end out of the power bank (through the -X end window) and plugs it into the computer. Keep the power cable (port 2) unplugged while flashing.

SG90 dimensions are nominal (body 22.8 x 12.2 x 22.7, tab span 32.2, shaft about 5.5 mm off body centre, shaft tip about 31 mm above the base), not measured. The TEST ONLY coupon checks the pocket and the horn groove. Assumed: a larger PWM pulse turns the shaft counter-clockwise seen from the shaft side. The firmware sign table and the case report confirm this, and the /rap page shows it at assembly.

Knee servo position and the leg geometry are case-owned targets, not sealed. The case team reports the actual neutral pose, the mirror error (≤ 0.5 mm / 1° on STEP) and the hip/knee range (target ≥ ±25°) for firmware reconciliation at integration.

Targets owned by teams, not sealed limits: shelf at z 18-21, lid thickness 3 mm, window and poke-hole sizes, cable slack zones, PCA corner holes, servo pulse range (about 500-2400 µs), heartbeat timing, LED brightness cap, gait speeds and step sizes, and plate layout. The case still has to respect every hard brief limit (≤ 12 printed parts, ≤ 12 M3 screws from the owner's M3x6/8/12/20 + nuts, ≤ 8 h print and ≤ 4 h30 per plate, ≤ 220 g plastic, ≤ 2 plates, robot < 500 g including the pack; walls ≥ 3 mm, posts/tabs ≥ 6x6 or Ø8 and ≤ 3x their smallest side, fillets ≥ 2 mm).

Estimated mass: 8 SG90 about 72 g + pack ≤ 120 g + electronics about 25 g + wiring about 20 g + screws about 15 g + plastic ≤ 220 g, about 472 g. Close to the 500 g limit, so the case team reports the actual slicer mass.

Dummy KiCad PCB: 30 x 20 x 1.6 mm, two Ø3.2 holes at (±10, 0). Its pad set and schematic are owned by the board team. It does not represent the robot wiring. Native ERC/DRC must pass without weakening any rule.
Images in prompts/assets are references only and never used as dimensions. The personal photos IMG_243*.jpg stay local and must not be pushed.
Integration reconciles all module envelopes with the real LILYGO STEP, the PCA9685 module and the owner's parts. Nothing has been hardware tested (hardwareTested = false).

coordinateFrame.axes: +X = front of the robot (the front hip servos, ports end of the power bank faces -X); +Y = left side when viewed from above with the front pointing away from you; +Z = up (the lid side). Right-handed. Seen from above: front-left (FL) = +X+Y, front-right (FR) = +X-Y, rear-left (RL) = -X+Y, rear-right (RR) = -X-Y.
coordinateFrame.origin: ROBOT BODY FRAME: X/Y origin at the centre of the 126 x 75 mm body footprint; z = 0 on the underside of the bottom part (dáy). Every module position is the centre of that module's bounding box in this frame, at the neutral standing pose. EXCEPTION: board.outlineMm and board.mounts describe the DUMMY KiCad PCB in its own local frame (origin at the PCB outline centre, same axis directions, z = 0 on top copper). That PCB is NEVER placed in the robot and has no position in the body frame.

firmwareBehavior: Target ESP32-S3 on the LILYGO T-Display-S3 non-touch (16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM per the 2024-04-29 schematic). Non-blocking main loop. All GPIO numbers come from one config header that matches the pins in this contract.

Power-up: drive GPIO15 HIGH and the backlight on GPIO38. Start the PCA9685 at I2C 0x40, 400 kHz, 50 Hz, on SDA = GPIO18 and SCL = GPIO17. Enable the servos one at a time, about 300 ms apart, in the order hips then knees, going straight to the standing pose. Stand still and never walk without a command.

First boot, or no saved Wi-Fi: start an open soft-AP 'CuaRobot-XXXX' (last 4 hex digits of the MAC) at 192.168.4.1. Run a DNS captive portal so the phone opens the setup page by itself. The screen shows a Wi-Fi join QR (WIFI:T:nopass;S:CuaRobot-XXXX;;) with a short Vietnamese instruction.

Setup page lists nearby networks (scan), with SSID chosen from the list and a password field. On submit, try the home network for about 15 s. Wrong password or timeout: go back to the AP and the first QR, and show a plain Vietnamese error on both the screen and the page (e.g. 'Sai mật khẩu Wi-Fi, thử lại nhé'). Never log or echo the password.

Success: save SSID and password in NVS, stop the AP, and show a second QR (http://<ip>/) plus the IP text and 'Đã vào Wi-Fi'. Later boots join automatically from NVS. If the saved network is unreachable, show a Vietnamese status and keep retrying. Fallback to the AP after a timeout is a firmware-owned choice.
Holding BOOT (GPIO0) for about 8 s erases the saved Wi-Fi from NVS and restarts into first-boot mode. Show a visible countdown in Vietnamese while it is held.

Control page at / fits a phone screen and needs no external libraries or internet (HTML/CSS/JS inline in the firmware). It has 8 direction buttons (tới, lui, trái, phải, xiên tới trái, xiên tới phải, xiên lui trái, xiên lui phải) and 1 light on/off button. No login or password.

Hold to move: while a button is held the page sends a command plus a heartbeat about every 200 ms (WebSocket or HTTP, firmware's choice). Release, page hidden, or no heartbeat for about 600 ms makes the robot stop smoothly back to standing. Losing the connection always stops it.

Gait is ported from Kame32 (oscillator-based) and non-blocking. Left/right is sideways crab walking. If the gait simulation shows sideways walking does not work, left/right become turn-in-place and README says so. Diagonals combine the forward/back and sideways phases.

Current smoothing: all joint targets are interpolated with a speed limit and acceleration ramps, no step changes. No more than 4 servos make large moves at the same instant (stagger the leg phases). If the power bank still cuts out, README advises a lower speed setting or a different power bank.

Joint convention: physical servo angle 90° (about 1500 µs) is neutral standing, with each leg on the 45° diagonal. A per-channel direction sign table (default knee: FL +1, RR +1, FR -1, RL -1; hip: positive = shaft counter-clockwise seen from above) converts gait angles to servo angles. The case team confirms the signs in its mechanical report. The trim only corrects horn spline alignment and never hides a geometry error.

'Ráp' (assembly) page at /rap: one button sends all 8 servos to 90° so the horns can be fitted, then per-joint +/- buttons in 1° steps (limited to ±15°), with Save to NVS and reset-trim. Movement is disabled while this page is active.
Light: one on/off toggle for the WS2812 bar on GPIO21 (8 LEDs, GRB, 800 kHz via RMT). All 8 LEDs are the same colour so the light is even. Off at boot.
Screen shows only the QR codes, the web address, the Wi-Fi status and Vietnamese error text. No other UI.

Deliverables: source code, a binary that builds, and host tests for the web handlers, QR payloads, the Wi-Fi state machine with a mocked radio, heartbeat timeout and stop, the direction-to-gait mapping and NVS trim. Never flash, run motors or touch hardware.

modules.interface: Slim USB power bank with 2 USB-A outputs, owner-bought. Lies flat on the floor (z 3-18) with its long side along X. Ports face -X into a plug zone at x -60..-37, z 3-18, which holds the L-cable plug and the USB-A power-cable plug. The -X end wall has a finger window to unplug both plugs. The +X end is open so the pack slides out toward +X for charging. Held with a zip tie or strap, no screws. A shelf at z 18-21 sits above it.

ESP32-S3 board with a 1.9 inch ST7789 170x320 screen facing up (+Z). Its long side runs along X, with the USB-C and both top buttons at the -X end. The envelope assumes the clear shell is on. The box runs z 21-44 and includes the downward pin headers and the Dupont plug housings under the PCB. The screen glass sits just under the lid. Lid window target: 24 x 44 mm centred near (2, 19). BOOT poke holes (Ø3, target) over both end buttons near (-29, 10) and (-29, 28). The L-shaped USB-C plug zone is x -47..-33 at y 19. Held by a printed cradle plus a zip tie, no screws.

Adafruit-layout 16-channel PWM board (or a same-layout clone). Lies flat on the shelf with its long side along X. The servo header row (channels 0-15) faces -Y, toward the outer wall. The screw terminal faces +Y and must be reachable from above when the lid is off. The 6-pin end headers are at the ±X ends. Height includes the upright servo plugs (z 21-43). Mounted in a printed pocket with a zip tie. The module's 4 corner holes (Ø2.5, about 56 x 19 mm pattern, unmeasured) are optional.

8-LED WS2812 bar, LEDs facing up (+Z), long side along X, centred in X so the light is spread evenly front to back. It sits directly under a lid diffuser zone at least 0.8 mm thin. Pads at the input end. Held in a printed slot or rib, no screws.

SG90 in a pocket printed into the bottom part, shaft vertical pointing +Z. Body 12.2 (X) x 22.8 (Y) x 22.7 (Z) sitting on the shelf at z 21. Mounting tabs run along Y. The output shaft is toward the outer (+Y) end at (53.9, 23.9). The top boss passes through the lid. The horn and leg sit above the lid and are not counted in the body envelope. Retained by the shared clamp bar with M3 screws.
Mirror of FL across y = 0, placed as FL turned 180° (the shaft stays toward the outer wall). Shaft at (53.9, -23.9).
Mirror of FL across x = 0. Shaft at (-53.9, 23.9).
FL turned 180° about Z. Shaft at (-53.9, -23.9).

modules.id: SERVO_KNEES x4 (PCA ch1 FL, ch3 FR, ch5 RL, ch7 RR)
modules.interface: Each SG90 sits in a pocket printed into leg part 1, with its shaft horizontal. The values are a TARGET envelope per knee servo: centre at a radius of about 30 mm from its hip shaft, on the 45° diagonal outward from the body centre (FL about (75, 45, 40), the others mirrored by sign). The exact pose is owned by the case team and reconciled at integration. The cable runs back to the PCA9685 with a slack loop across the hip joint.
Pads and two Ø3.2 holes only, no parts fitted. Silkscreen reads 'BOARD GIẢ - KHÔNG ĐẶT - KHÔNG ĐẶT VÀO ROBOT'. NOT in the robot; position given in its own local frame only.

powerRails.name: VBUS_MCU_5V
powerRails.source: Power bank USB port 1 -> owner-bought 90-degree (L-shaped) USB-A to USB-C cable -> LILYGO T-Display-S3 USB-C VBUS. Powers only the LILYGO. For flashing, the owner moves this cable's USB-A end from the power bank to a computer.

powerRails.name: 3V3
powerRails.source: Regulator built into the LILYGO T-Display-S3, taken from its header pin labelled 3V. Its only load in this contract is the PCA9685 VCC logic pin.

powerRails.name: V_SERVO_5V
powerRails.source: Power bank USB port 2 -> ready-made USB-A male to 2-wire cable (red = +5V, black = GND) -> PCA9685 blue screw terminal V+ / GND. Powers all 8 SG90s through their own plugs, and the WS2812 bar through the PCA9685 6-pin end header V+ pin.

powerRails.name: GND
powerRails.source: Common ground. The power bank's two ports share ground, and one Dupont wire runs from a LILYGO GND header pin to the PCA9685 end header GND pin. The servo plug brown wires and the LED bar GND go to PCA9685 GND.

tasks.board: BOARD TEAM (design/ only): native KiCad project for the DUMMY board only. A 30 x 20 x 1.6 mm, 2-layer outline exactly as in board.outlineMm, with two Ø3.2 NPTH/PTH holes at (±10, 0). Contents: solder pads and mounting holes, no fitted parts. The schematic is correct for this board alone: pad symbols and the mounting holes, with any pads used as solder landing points tied to named nets. No power bank, servos, PCA9685, LILYGO or LED module in the schematic. Silkscreen and title block read 'BOARD GIẢ - KHÔNG ĐẶT - KHÔNG ĐẶT VÀO ROBOT'. Pad sizes and nets are the board team's choice. Run native ERC/DRC until clean without weakening rules, and publish the packet. Do not touch firmware/ or case/.
tasks.case: CASE TEAM (case/ only): full handwired-robot mechanics in the contract body frame. Parts: 1 bottom (dáy) with built-in pockets for the power bank, LILYGO, PCA9685, LED bar and 4 hip SG90s, plus cable routes and slack space. 1 lid with the screen window, BOOT poke holes and LED diffuser. Shared M3 clamp bar(s) for the hip servos. 4 legs × 2 solid filleted parts, with the knee SG90 pocket and a press-fit SG90 horn groove. Respect every module envelope and port/plug zone above, and all hard brief limits. Use only the owner's M3x6/8/12/20 + nuts and the SG90 bag screws, every hole labelled and reachable with a screwdriver. No slender free-standing posts. Deliver: mirror-symmetry and collision/range checks on the STEP at neutral, a post/tab cross-section report, mechanical.json with nativePCBCheckerApplies: false, the TEST ONLY coupon and MATING_TEST, STEP/STL per part, one Print-all 3MF with named plates (≤ 2, ≤ 4 h30 each, long side along X, sliced with the owner's PETG 0.20 / 2 walls / 7% grid / tree-auto profile), fastener_map.csv, the phone-readable overview (Đủ bộ → Bước 1..N with a wiring step and a 'Vít/tán bước này' card on each step, Chi tiết collapsed), case/PRINTED-INVENTORY.md, CHECKLIST-RAP.md mechanical items and BOM. Report the actual servo direction signs and the knee neutral pose for firmware reconciliation. Never send a print.
tasks.firmware: FIRMWARE TEAM (firmware/ only): ESP32-S3 firmware for the LILYGO T-Display-S3 non-touch. Toolchain is the team's choice (ESP-IDF or Arduino-ESP32 via PlatformIO, version pinned, caches git-ignored). Implement every firmwareBehavior item using exactly the contract pins: I2C on 18/17, PCA9685 at 0x40 on channels 0-7 per the mapping, WS2812 on GPIO21, BOOT on GPIO0, LCD on the listed onboard pins; never GPIO16 or GPIO43. Deliver the source code, a binary that builds, and host tests (web handlers, QR payloads, Wi-Fi state machine, heartbeat stop, direction-to-gait, NVS trim). Run a kinematic gait simulation for sideways walking and hip/knee range ≥ ±25° using the contract's hip positions and the knee target. Also deliver firmware/WIRING.md in Vietnamese with a drawing (every Dupont/plug/terminal connection from-to with colours, power bank port 1/2, no measuring) and the firmware/flashing sections of README.md, all of which the lead merges. Never flash or run hardware.
